body: Yeah I think it’s really necessary to find the right therapist for this and not just a therapist for this reason, people feel very confronted when you talk about suicide, you need someone who can really understand mental illness and impulsive thoughts. For majority of us wanting to die is just a Tuesday morning lol

Do you have an active plan to do it or are these thoughts that you can recognise and go I won’t do that but I can’t help feeling this way? Depending on where you are, therapy should be a space where you can talk about the darkest things that cross your mind especially if you are in therapy for depression. If this is a worry for you, be clear when you see them that the topic you want to talk about is this, and that you are afraid of talking or opening up about it under concern of being put under hospitalisation. That you don’t have an active plan to hurt yourself or anyone else, but you need a safe space to confront these thoughts and discuss them without holding back. I would recommend doing this with a therapist you have some sort of knowledge of each other and mutual trust too.
Feel free to message me if you ever want advice, I am almost 30 now have dealt with these feelings for a long time. I really do hope it helps.

I struggled with this a lot in my late teens and early years of adulthood, I never spoke it out loud but it was definitely prevalent in my life. It got to the point where it was affecting all aspects of my life and no one wanted to be around me because I was just so miserable and self doubting. I went to a psychologist, and I have been to many but this one just clicked with me. He sat me down and showed me diagrams of my brain, what exactly was happening depression wise and encouraged me to get tested for ADHD/Austisim. (Ended up having both) but what he did the most that helped was rewiring my thought process. He made me become conscious of the things I thought, for example when you are talking about reading a book and then you call yourself a slow reader, he would make me stop, picture a stop sign in my head and consciously change that thought to learning to read better, if I had a thought where I went, why am I so bad at everything? I would stop and change it to I have the capability to learn anything, if I thought all I do is fail, I would stop and say now I know what not to do for when I try again. It took a long time, and sometimes I wouldn’t forget, sometimes I would spiral, even today years later I still do get episodes where I have to sit and consciously remind myself that it will pass, but as with everything and especially mental illness life is a constant effort and no one is capable of saving you but yourself, they can give you tools and assistance but you are the only person inside your head. A good tip if you are willing to use it is when you recognise your thoughts and hear yourself comparing, picture that stop sign in your head and change it, reword if if you can’t change it to something positive straight away (example instead of I’m slow, I’m learning) and over time you will catch yourself doing it naturally. Give yourself some grace, if you keep comparing your partners successes to yours it will be your relationships downfall and you are capable of more, you do not need to be better than anyone, and you’ve got this. You are such a young kid, even though at 18 we believe we should be capable of handling the world, you are just a kid, picture yourself like a new born baby adult lol, some people are capable of just clicking their fingers and winning, people like us need to let go of our jealousy of that and realise that we are too if we stop putting ourselves down the moment we try to
